items.prose: Using petroleum jelly on the 29/42 boiling flask joint failed as solvent vapors dissolved the grease. The leached hydrocarbons carried over into the condenser, contaminating five liters of pharmaceutical ether with an oily residue.

Sixteen hours of vacuum distillation at 220°C polymerized the silicone high-vacuum grease into an insoluble, glass-hard silicon dioxide film. The standard taper joints fused into a monolithic unit that resisted all organic solvents.

Under high vacuum (10^-3 torr) and 240°C head temperature, low-molecular-weight fractions of the fluorinated grease sublimated. The dry joint developed microscopic leak channels that admitted atmospheric air into the sensitive radioisotope trap.

An operator rubbed candle wax onto the 24/40 joint of a two-liter boiling flask. As the ethanol began boiling at 78°C, the wax melted into liquid oil; the heavy flask slipped out of its three-finger clamp and shattered on the bench burner.

Evaporation of water from a boric acid and glycerin lubricant formulation caused sharp orthoboric acid crystals to precipitate. Rotating the joint ground abrasive furrows into the frosted mating surfaces, destroying vacuum tightness.

Inserting a 0.05mm PTFE taper sleeve carelessly caused a longitudinal wrinkle across the sealing face. The crease opened a 2 torr vacuum bypass, venting volatile chloroform anesthetic vapors into the subterranean laboratory.

Distilling concentrated 40% sodium hydroxide lye without Teflon sleeves allowed alkaline liquid to capillary-wick into the ungreased joint. The lye dissolved the borosilicate glass into sticky sodium silicate, chemically welding the flask to the condenser forever.
